The dummy's role in offensive warding implies a constraint-based interaction model where player kinetic energy is absorbed by a fixed point. This aligns with classical mechanics where impulse equals change in momentum. The charging machine introduces a dynamic element—accelerated mass interacting with stationary or slower-moving targets—modeling real-world collision dynamics. Ground padding introduces a dissipative term, modifying the energy balance post-impact. The dual nature of these tools—offensive and defensive—reflects a symmetry in training objectives, suggesting an underlying duality in tactical planning. Failure modes arise from inadequate padding or improper dummy construction, leading to injury or reduced training fidelity. The mathematical structure supports Bayesian updating of performance metrics based on empirical data from repeated interactions.
